overview: Both are gonadotropins from the anterior pituitary controlling reproduction, but they trigger different key events in the cycle.
genZNote: FSH: gets the follicle growing. LH: delivers the final trigger for ovulation.

aspects.label: Main Role in Females
aspects.valueA: Stimulates growth and maturation of ovarian follicles.
aspects.valueB: Triggers ovulation (the LH surge) and forms/maintains the corpus luteum.

aspects.label: Main Role in Males
aspects.valueA: Stimulates Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis.
aspects.valueB: Stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone.

aspects.label: Timing in Menstrual Cycle
aspects.valueA: Rises in the early follicular phase.
aspects.valueB: Peaks sharply mid-cycle (the LH surge), directly triggering ovulation.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The mid-cycle LH surge is the direct trigger for ovulation — a heavily tested detail in the menstrual cycle timeline.
overlay.memoryTrick: FSH = Follicle-Stimulating (grows the follicle). LH = triggers ovulation (Luteinizing = forms the corpus luteum afterward).
overlay.commonMisconception: FSH and LH are not sex-specific hormones — both are secreted in males and females, just acting on different target cells (Sertoli vs Leydig cells in males).
